issue.title: Totals endpoint times out on a report with 1.6 million transactions
issue.body:
`GET /reports/:id/totals` for our "Main operating account since 2019" report,
about 1.6 million transactions, takes 30 to 40 seconds when it works and
returns `500 internal error` about half the time. The server log for the
failures says:

    {"level":"error","msg":"unhandled error","err":{"type":"DatabaseError","code":"57014","message":"canceling statement due to statement timeout"}}

Totals for our smaller reports come back at once, and the process's memory
jumps by over a gigabyte during each call. We only need the three numbers per
currency, not the rows.

input.title: Compute report totals in SQL instead of loading every row
input.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

The GET /reports/:id/totals handler calls transactionRepo.listForReport(report) with no limit, which loads every matching transaction into memory, then totalsByCurrency() reduces them in JavaScript. For a 1.6 million row report this is slow, uses over a gigabyte, and hits the 15 s DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS.

Proposed change: add a repo method in src/db/repos/transactionRepo.ts that returns per-currency count, inflow and outflow using GROUP BY currency with SUM(...) FILTER (WHERE amount >= 0) and FILTER (WHERE amount < 0), applying the same account, date range and category filters as listForReport. The totals handler should call that method and drop the in-memory totalsByCurrency reduction. The response shape stays the same.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The totals handler loads every matching transaction with transactionRepo.listForReport and no limit, then sums them in totalsByCurrency(). On a 1.6 million row report that is what exceeds the 15 s statement timeout and inflates memory. docs/PERFORMANCE.md already recommends aggregating in SQL for any endpoint that can see more than a few hundred thousand rows. The draft pull request moves the per-currency sums into a SQL GROUP BY, so only three numbers per currency come back.
